title: Ordinary evaluation transport across the open-site equivalence
statement: Let X be a scheme and U an open [def-pc-scheme]. Let P,F be complexes of modules on the over-U site [def-pur-hom-complex]. Assume Hom(P,-) preserves quasi-isomorphisms, Hom(P,O_U[0]) is K-flat [def-pc-kflat-complex], and F is K-injective [def-pur-kinjective-complex]. Let f:Tot(F tensor Hom(P,O_U[0])) to Hom(P,F) obey [def-pc-ordinary-evaluation-data]. Let L be the concrete Modules.overEquiv U functor [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits], T its degreewise complex functor, P'=T(P), F'=T(F), O'=O_(U.toScheme)[0] and V'=Hom(P',O'). There are chain isomorphisms t:T(Tot(F tensor Hom(P,O_U[0]))) to Tot(F' tensor V') and b:T(Hom(P,F)) to Hom(P',F'). Hom(P',-) preserves all quasi-isomorphisms, V' is K-flat, F' is K-injective, and t.inverse;T(f);b satisfies [def-pc-scheme-ordinary-evaluation-formula]. All complexes P',F' are the actual degreewise images; no derived tensor, RHom, or derived evaluation square is asserted.

proof.text: Reindex local tensor pure sections and the unit action along Modules.overEquiv. The inverse reindexing is the inverse map. Preserve the tensor coproducts and the degree-zero unit; additivity identifies the signed total differential. This constructs the chain isomorphism t, not merely a derived comparison.

Apply internalHom_overEquiv to each pair of terms. Its pre- and postcomposition naturality, together with product preservation, identifies the Hom differentials and gives b. Use the exact inverse to transport acyclicity and quasi-isomorphisms; conjugate Hom(P,-) to get hhom on P'. The tensor comparison in both directions transports K-flatness. The Hom homotopy comparison and the exact inverse transport K-injectivity.

Follow t.inverse;T(f);b by every product projection and precede it by every tensor summand inclusion. The first two steps send those inclusions, projections, symmetries, associators and the unit action to their canonical comparisons. The given component equation therefore becomes the identical one on the scheme site. The r+q=0 branch uses the transported single-unit isomorphism; the other branch remains zero.

theorem exists_ordinaryEvaluation_over_transport (X : Scheme.{u}) (U : X.Opens)
    (P F : CochainComplex (localEvaluationModules X U) ℤ)
    (hhom : ∀ (M M' : CochainComplex (localEvaluationModules X U) ℤ) (t : M ⟶ M'),
      QuasiIso t → QuasiIso (((homComplexFunctor (R := X.sheaf.over U)).obj (op P)).map t))
    (hdual : (localEvaluationDual X U P).IsKFlat)
    (f : localEvaluationTensor X U P F ⟶ homComplex (R := X.sheaf.over U) P F)
    (hf : IsLocalOrdinaryEvaluation X U P F f) [F.IsKInjective] :
    let L := Equivalence.functor
      (C := SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over U))
      (D := SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings U.toScheme.toRingedSpace))
      (Scheme.Modules.overEquiv U)
    let T := L.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)
    let P' := T.obj P
    let F' := T.obj F
    let O' := (HomologicalComplex.single _ (.up ℤ) 0).obj
      (𝟙_ (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings U.toScheme.toRingedSpace)))
    let D' := homComplex (R := U.toScheme.sheaf) P' O'
    ∃ t : T.obj (localEvaluationTensor X U P F) ≅ pullbackTensorTotal U.toScheme F' D',
      ∃ b : T.obj (homComplex (R := X.sheaf.over U) P F) ≅
          homComplex (R := U.toScheme.sheaf) P' F',
        (∀ (M M' : CochainComplex
            (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings U.toScheme.toRingedSpace)) ℤ) (a : M ⟶ M'),
          QuasiIso a →
            QuasiIso (((homComplexFunctor (R := U.toScheme.sheaf)).obj (op P')).map a)) ∧
        D'.IsKFlat ∧ CochainComplex.IsKInjective F' ∧
        IsSchemeOrdinaryEvaluation U.toScheme P' F' (t.inv ≫ T.map f ≫ b.hom)
